clue.text: Small detached place brings in rent

definitions.meaning: a tiny island standing apart from the mainland
read as two words, '...': a property that ... earns its owner rent

explanation.surface: A little detached house pays its way with a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition only works with the answer split as IS LET: a flat that is let brings in rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island is a place cut off from everything around it.

clue.text: Bobby, grabbing seat and sitting in it, gains nothing thereby

indicators.note: gains says the next piece is added on at the end
the policeman with his seat sits inside the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the officer grabs the seat, holding it inside himself

parts.note: a bobby is a British policeman, PC for police constable
a sofa is a seat
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A policeman takes a sofa, sits in it and gets nothing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts SOFA in PC; 'sitting in' puts that in IT; 'gains' adds O. Bobby is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by that very fact, as a direct result.

clue.text: Cut chapter, in a way

indicators.note: in places the chapter inside the road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow way or road

explanation.surface: A section of the road has been cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons lance a boil, cutting it open.

clue.text: It's an effort for Virginia to wear scent

indicators.note: the scent wears the state, holding it inside like a garment

parts.note: a trail is a scent followed by hounds
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A woman named Virginia finds putting on perfume hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is hard labour or painful toil.

clue.text: Room to bring young lady back — an easy catch

indicators.note: back tells us to turn the word for the young lady round

parts.note: a deb is a debutante, a young society lady
in cricket a sitter is a catch so simple it should never be dropped

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that bringing a girl home was as easy as a dropped-into-the-hands catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns DEB into BED. A sitter is cricket slang for a very easy catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-room flat serving as both bedroom and living space is a type of rented room.

clue.text: Diplomat inducted into the highest order

indicators.note: the diplomat is brought inside the word for highest

parts.note: the best is the highest in quality
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy is admitted into the highest order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or instruction someone gives.

clue.text: Guide cried out "The Peak!"

indicators.note: out signals the word cried is put out of order

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill or peak, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A tour leader shouted on reaching the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges CRIED into DIREC; TOR is a craggy hilltop in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A director guides or steers an enterprise.

clue.text: Synchronised popular exercise has got accepted

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: the word has is received inside the exercise letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: A trendy fitness class has been approved for coordinated workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: Two waves that rise and fall together are synchronised.

clue.text: Forecast depression will lift, due to change in low behaviour

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting reads the forecast and depression upwards

parts.note: a tip is a forecast, as of a winner
a rut is a groove or depression in the ground

indicators.note: to change puts the word due into a new order

explanation.surface: A weather report says a low-pressure area will clear because of a shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will lift' reverses TIPRUT to TURPIT; 'to change' turns DUE into UDE. The weather vocabulary disguises the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpitude is depravity, wickedness: base conduct.

clue.text: Material managed to cover most of you

indicators.note: the managed word covers, enclosing the rest

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a shop

indicators.note: most of drops the last letter of the word you

explanation.surface: Someone managed to cover nearly all of you with fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is an artificial silk-like fabric.

clue.text: Foolishly burnt as he laid out?

definitions.text: Foolishly burnt as he laid out?

indicators.note: done foolishly, the letters are arranged in a silly new order

explanation.surface: A man stupidly got scorched while lying stretched out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foolishly' rearranges BURNT AS HE; the whole clue also describes someone who lay in the sun too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lies out in strong sunshine carelessly ends up with a burn.

clue.text: Deal evasively with composer

definitions.meaning: to fend off or sidestep a question or blow
Sir Hubert ..., English composer of Jerusalem

explanation.surface: Someone handles a famous musician's questions slyly.
explanation.definitionFit: To deflect a question is to avoid it; Hubert Parry wrote the music for Jerusalem.

clue.text: Club with no entrance fee? That's not logical talk

definitions.meaning: a society costing nothing to join, read literally
the psychoanalytic technique of saying whatever comes to mind, without reasoning

explanation.surface: A free-to-join club is mocked for its rambling, illogical chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is a society one joins, and the therapist's technique is speech that follows no logic.

clue.text: Heroic nurse smuggles bible into part of prison

indicators.note: a cell smuggling something in has it secreted inside its walls
into says the bible goes inside the prison room

parts.note: a cell is one room of a prison
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A brave nurse sneaks a Bible into a prisoner's quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Cavell was a British nurse executed in 1915 for helping Allied soldiers escape occupied Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Cavell is remembered as a heroine of the First World War nursing service.

clue.text: Totter and leave, sick at heart

indicators.note: the sick word is at the centre of the leave word

parts.note: vacate means leave a place
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone staggers and goes off, feeling sick inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver unsteadily is to totter, physically or in opinion.

clue.text: Independence UK experienced in 1964?

parts.note: Sir Alec Douglas-Home was Prime Minister in 1964, so Britain was governed by him that year; the phrase also means self-government

explanation.surface: A history question about some British freedom gained in 1964.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas-Home (pronounced 'Hume') was Prime Minister until October 1964, so the UK lived under his rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-government for a region within a state is the political term this phrase names.

clue.text: Assisted deputy up and went outside

indicators.note: the went word sits outside the deputy word

parts.note: exited means went out

indicators.note: in a down clue up reads the deputy abbreviation upwards

explanation.surface: A deputy was helped up and stepped outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses DEP to PED, placed in EXITED.
explanation.definitionFit: To expedite is to hasten progress, which helps it along.

clue.text: New routine devised to discover subatomic particle

indicators.note: devised means the routine's letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: A scientist's fresh method helps detect a tiny particle.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrino is an electrically neutral subatomic particle.

clue.text: Short examination about Anglicanism completed

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject
CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church
over means finished, completed

explanation.surface: A brief look into the Anglican faith has been finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick inspection or cursory look is a brief examination.

clue.text: Manage to get abroad, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the answer sounds like the word for abroad

parts.note: overseas means abroad

explanation.surface: Someone contrives to travel abroad, so the story goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise is to manage or watch over.

clue.text: Party emerges from grave upheaval

indicators.note: the answer comes out of the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: A celebration bursts out of a serious upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: A rave-up is a lively, noisy party, especially British slang.

clue.text: A requirement is entered for strong flavour

indicators.note: is entered means the word is goes inside the requirement

parts.note: a need is a requirement

explanation.surface: A recipe insists a powerful flavouring be added.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise seed has a pungent liquorice taste.

clue.text: Do favour force

definitions.meaning: to compel, as in ... to leave

explanation.surface: Doing someone a kindness under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Accommodating someone is a kindness; being compelled is being forced.

clue.text: I blessed the wall, newly-built with good foundations

indicators.note: the wall's letters are put together again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A priest blesses a freshly built wall standing on solid foundations.
explanation.definitionFit: Something firmly founded is securely settled and long-lasting.

clue.text: Old man finds head covering extremely hot

parts.note: a wig covers the head

indicators.note: extremely takes the first and last letters of hot

explanation.surface: An elderly man's hairpiece is far too warm.
explanation.walkthrough: Wight is an archaic word for a person or creature.
explanation.definitionFit: In old English, a wight was a human being, a fellow.

clue.text: Impetuous, set off to the unknown

parts.note: head means set off towards, as in head for home
y is an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone rashly sets out for an unexplored land.
explanation.definitionFit: Heady means rash, hot-headed, impulsive.

clue.text: Consumes fowl with last of dressing passed round

indicators.note: passed round turns the bird and the letter backwards together

parts.note: a swan is a large water fowl

indicators.note: the final letter of the word dressing is taken

explanation.surface: A diner eats a bird with the last of the stuffing handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: SWAN + G (end of 'dressing') is SWANG; 'passed round' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnaw is to eat away at something bit by bit.

clue.text: He wanders around the point in one incoherent speech

indicators.note: in places the point within the other pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rant is a wild, ranting speech
a tine is a point or prong, as of a fork

explanation.surface: A man roams about, sharp in one rambling tirade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' belongs to the definition, not a container: the point goes in I+RANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A traveller who moves from place to place is a wanderer.

clue.text: It follows that cattle died out in extremes of temperature

indicators.note: in puts the cattle word within the temperature letters
the first and last letters of temperature are taken
out says the word for died is removed

parts.note: Hereford is a breed of beef cattle from the English county

explanation.surface: Livestock perished in a heatwave or a cold snap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' takes the D for 'died' from the cattle breed, and 'extremes of' gives T and E. Hereford is an English county that gives its name to red-and-white beef cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word introduces a logical consequence: thus, hence.

clue.text: Spirit from the wood is unsweetened, notice

parts.note: dry wine is not sweet
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A woodland sprite is described as sour and announced in a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a tree nymph lives in the forest.
